subject: Request: SLA addendum + order form language for CoreHealth (latency SLO)
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@corehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: CoreHealth Procurement <procurement@corehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA addendum for latency commitments (thread kick-off)

Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we scope enterprise contract language we need a short addendum to the MSA that covers a tighter 99.5% uptime for our production endpoints and a latency objective (p95 < 300ms for generation requests up to 512 tokens). Procurement asked that this be surfaced as an SLA exhibit and reflected in the order form (so it travels with the committed capacity line item).

Can Redwood provide:
- A redline of your standard SLA adding the latency objective + any monitoring/measurement definitions
- Suggested order form language we can include in our procurement system (we prefer short exhibit wording rather than lengthy annexes)
- Any constraints or exceptions (e.g., scheduled maintenance windows, force majeure, agreed mitigation credits)

We'd like to close this in the next two weeks. Attaching our draft scorecard for context.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Torres
Head of Platform Ops | CoreHealth Analytics

Attachment: CH_production_metrics_v1.xlsx (attachment stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@corehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum for latency commitments (thread kick-off)

Michael —

Appreciate the clear ask. We've pulled a draft addendum and a concise order-form snippet for your procurement team to review. High level: we can commit to a 99.5% monthly availability SLO on the dedicated model endpoints and provide a measurement definition for p95 latency for requests <=512 tokens, with the caveat that cold-starts during scale-up are excluded for a 10 minute per-incident window.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll attach the redline (SLA_Addendum_v1) and a marked-up order form language for your legal/procurement to comment on.
2) Laura (cc'd) from Legal will propose any guardrail language around credits and measurement windows.
3) If those look OK, Jonas can sign off for order-level exceptions once we align runbook/monitoring.

Deliverables attached: CoreHealth_Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v1.docx (redline), Redwood_OrderForm_markup.pdf (suggested text), and an internal monitoring runbook we’d use for outage reconciliation.

I’ll make time for a short call with your ops team if you want to walk the measurement definitions.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0127

Attachments: CoreHealth_Redwood_SLA_Addendum_v1.docx, Redwood_OrderForm_markup.pdf, SLA-monitoring-runbook.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@corehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum for latency commitments (thread kick-off)

Michael / Ben —

Quick note from Legal on the draft addendum: thanks for the clarity in the ask. A couple points we want to surface before redlines proceed:

- Measurement definition: we define p95 over all successful responses measured at the egress gateway in the customer's chosen region. We'll map this back to the order form.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (we propose 4 hours/month), third-party infra outages (e.g., cloud provider incidents), and force majeure should be standard. We will add language to cap monthly credits to avoid unlimited exposure.
- Credits: propose a tiered credit schedule (example in the redline). For p95 latency breaches that are outside of emergency maintenance, we can offer prorated credits up to a defined maximum of 20% of monthly fees for repeated failures.

One ask from our side: before formal accountability we need to confirm runbook access. Can CoreHealth grant read-only visibility into the Redwood monitoring dashboard for the endpoints covered by this order? That will help expedite dispute resolution.

I'll attach our marked-up redline; Ben, please confirm you are comfortable with the proposed exclusion windows so we can send back to CoreHealth.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Legal_redline.docx (internal redline)
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@corehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 13:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum for latency commitments (thread kick-off)

Laura —

Thanks, that's helpful. A few quick responses from Procurement/Ops:
- Read-only dashboard access: yes, we can accept read-only links for the covered endpoints; please spell out the exact metrics (availability %, p95 latency, request counts) so our security team can sign off on the tokenization/least-privilege configuration.
- Scheduled maintenance: 4 hours/month is acceptable provided we get advance notice (48 hours) for planned work.
- Credits: the tiered schedule is OK; procurement will also need a simple order form line that states the exception was approved and references the addendum (our procurement system relies on that reference).

We reviewed the redline and left a couple of inline comments in the PDF. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to go through the measurement definition. Are you available Thursday morning PT?

Best,
Michael

Attachment: CoreHealth_comments_orderform.pdf (annotation stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@corehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum for latency commitments (thread kick-off)

Team / Michael —

I've reviewed the proposed language and Laura's redline. Redwood is willing to approve the specific SLA addendum for CoreHealth on the condition that:

1) We set up the monitoring access (read-only dashboards + weekly SLO reports) and define a 72-hour remediation window before credits escalate.
2) The order form includes the exact exhibit identifier (Exhibit A: CoreHealth SLA Addendum) so procurement can reference it in their system.
3) We agree to a capped credit schedule (as per Laura's redline) and an initial 3-month operational review after go-live to ensure the p95 measurement histogram aligns with expectations.

Ben — please prepare the final order-form snippet and upload the revised addendum to DocuSign. Michael — once you confirm the dashboard metrics list (availability, p95 latency, per-endpoint request counts), we'll route the DocuSign packet for signatures.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
